Verbs 13–15 are human-device verbs (P8-D98): only a human principal on a device connection whose hello verified the kernel key may call them; they are not among law 3's twelve kernel verbs.

## Reserved (P8-D98)

- hello features: `journal.cursor`, `session.resume` — the kernel advertises none until it builds them; a missing feature refuses the dependent operation, never degrades it.
- `log.read` cursor: `{logId, seq}`; a cursor from another log is `BAD_REQUEST{reason:'cursor-epoch'}`.
- decisionSig v2: first line `gnomon:decision:v2`, used for `answer` decisions, carrying the answer digest.
- approve `scope` (TD-2026-10-20-294): `{kind:'exact'}` or `{kind:'prefix', prefix:[1-3 words]}`, only with `always` on a Bash permission card; a prefix scope signs the v2 layout whose last line is the scope digest (sha256 over canonicalJson of the scope).

## Kit and display rules

Kit blocks: `kit.Box`, `kit.Text`, `kit.List`, `kit.Table`, `kit.Markdown`, `kit.Diff`, `kit.Progress`, `kit.Button`, `kit.Image`, `kit.Canvas`. A block carries no actions; decision controls exist only on kernel-signed `card:v1.actions[]`.

Every string passes the §4.5 sanitizer (`sanitizeDisplayText`) before it is rendered; `conformance/display.v1.json` is normative and a conformant client reproduces it byte for byte.

- stripped (flag `hidden-chars`): U+00AD, U+034F, U+115F–U+1160, U+180E, U+200B–U+200D, U+2060–U+2064, U+3164, U+FEFF, U+FFA0, U+E0000–U+E007F, U+E0100–U+E01EF
- shown as glyphs (flag `bidi`): U+061C → ⟨ALM⟩, U+200E → ⟨LRM⟩, U+200F → ⟨RLM⟩, U+202A → ⟨LRE⟩, U+202B → ⟨RLE⟩, U+202C → ⟨PDF⟩, U+202D → ⟨LRO⟩, U+202E → ⟨RLO⟩, U+2066 → ⟨LRI⟩, U+2067 → ⟨RLI⟩, U+2068 → ⟨FSI⟩, U+2069 → ⟨PDI⟩
- every number is shown as `{n, of}` (`renderDenominator`); a bare count is refused.

## Conformance (`gnomon-client-conformance` v1)

`status` labels what a client declares in `hello{client.conformance}` as `declared`, never `passed`.

| check | a conformant client | spec | runner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hello.negotiate` | offers gnomon-rpc:v1; the kernel chooses it and reports clientApiId and kitId | §4.9 | run |
| `hello.unsupported` | offering no API the kernel speaks is refused UNSUPPORTED{data.offered} | §4.9 | run |
| `hello.server-sig` | verifies serverSig against the registered kernel key before auth | §4.9 | run |
| `hello.server-sig-mismatch` | a hello signed by any other key, or a genuine hello replayed from another connection (its clientNonce is not this one's), is refused locally and NO auth is sent | §4.9 | run |
| `auth.device` | authenticates with a device key (gnomon:auth:v1 over the negotiated hello) | §4.9 | run |
| `auth.device-refused` | an unregistered device key yields ONE AUTH refusal:v1 (-32001), surfaced as a refusal; the client keeps no connection | §4.9 | run |
| `auth.read-token` | authenticates a read token by proof of possession; write verbs are refused FORBIDDEN | §4.9, §5 | run |
| `auth.before-auth` | a known verb before auth yields AUTH{unauthenticated} and the connection closes | §4.9 | run |
| `auth.launch-token` | launch token → GUI token over the WebSocket transport | §4.9, §11.2 | catalogued, reported todo |
| `auth.reconnect` | Reconnect: {reconnect:true} raises presence and re-pins the kernel key | §4.9, D54 | catalogued, reported todo |
| `refusal.unknown-verb` | an unknown method yields UNKNOWN_VERB (-32601) carrying a valid refusal:v1 | §4.6, §4.9 | run |
| `refusal.bad-request` | malformed params yield BAD_REQUEST (-32600) carrying a valid refusal:v1 | §4.6, §4.9 | run |
| `subscribe.since` | log.read{follow, since} delivers the backlog then live rows, in seq order, without gaps | §4.9 | run |
| `subscribe.dropped` | survives socket.subscription.dropped by re-subscribing from since | §4.9 | catalogued, reported todo |
| `display.sanitize` | every string passes the §4.5 sanitizer incl. the Unicode rules (vectors) | §4.5 | run |
| `display.event-rows` | an unknown modns.* kind renders as an opaque {kind, principal, at} row, never dropped (vectors) | §4.9 | run |
| `display.denominator` | every number renders as {n, of}; a bare count is refused (vectors) | §9.1 | run |
| `cards.kernel-signed` | renders a card only from a kernel-signed approval.request; a forged one never appears | §12.8 G-CLI-03 | catalogued, reported todo |
